summary: ACCEPT, and TIME-CRITICAL: it repairs the external pager for the v2 boot hold, which is currently HELD on production and whose only automated escalation path is this script. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION ON THE BOX, NOT BY MOCK - a one-variable controlled pair against the live v2 process (MainPID 2079740), both outcomes reachable and the answer flips: the OLD form (sudo tr with the proc path as a third operand) exits 1 with the literal stderr 'tr: extra operand /proc/2079740/environ', because tr reads stdin and a third operand is an error; the NEW form (sudo cat of the same proc path) exits 0 and returns 9741 bytes, from which the key resolves to MAI_TAI_STRATEGY_SCHWAB_1M_V2_CW_ARMED_SEGMENT_SAFETY_ENABLED=true. That last step matters independently: it proves the real sudoers permits cat, so the fix is not one unusable command swapped for another - the exact failure mode of the bug being fixed. DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED: every live invocation was returning UNKNOWN. It could never false-green - sh() returns None on raise OR non-zero exit OR empty output and the caller treats None as UNKNOWN - so this was a fail-loud defect, not a silent mute. But a pager that always reports SAFETY FLAG UNKNOWN cannot report anything else, and on weekdays it would page continuously; a channel that always fires carries no information. THE KILLING TEST IS LOAD-BEARING, checked specifically because a mocked test can pass under both implementations: test_safety_flag_reads_proc_environ_as_nul_delimited_file asserts the exact command shape (calls[-1] equals the three-element sudo cat argv), so a revert to the tr form fails it by construction rather than by luck. Its payload is NUL-delimited and places a decoy OTHER_FLAG ahead of the real key, so naive prefix matching is caught too. FALLBACK RE-CHECKED, because my own earlier instruction broke this exact path once and created a pager mute: the absent-variable case returns None (UNKNOWN), not False (OFF). Absence cannot prove what the process inherited, so it must not resolve to a skip. Unchanged by this PR and confirmed still correct at the new head. NOT MEASURED: the unit tests mock sh(), so the shape assertion cannot prove the command works under the deployed sudoers - I closed that specific gap by executing it on the box as recorded above, but that is a point-in-time observation of one host, not a regression guard. If sudoers changes, no test catches it. DEPLOY NOTE: ops paths are NOT sync-only eligible; this needs an explicit copy to the box, and it does not require a v2 restart.
